records.name: Serial samples: a later sample against the same person's earlier one
questions: What exactly is this test comparing?
It compares a later sample from a person against an earlier sample from that same person, looking at every CpG site that both samples happened to measure.
Why use the person's own earlier sample instead of comparing against a panel of healthy people?
Because the person acts as their own reference point, so a separate healthy reference group isn't needed for this comparison.
Is this comparison based on some established statistical law?
No. It is a comparison rule of the pipeline: the person's earlier sample serves as the reference; IAM's Law does not enter it.
What are the limitations of this method that I should know about before relying on it?
Not yet recorded: the limits of serial comparison (how far apart the samples may be, and how depth differences are handled) have not been written for this instrument.
